packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 20 - unverified image reading (first reader, images only)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of this text before or during the reading. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001 to image-007 of this packet. I did nothing beyond the rules. I have not tried to identify the work or author.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 and image-004 are reduced overviews of the two faces of one small upright paper leaf; image-002 and image-003 are tiles of the text of the first face, image-005 to image-007 tiles of the second face.
- Single column on both faces. Verse, one verse per line, in rhymed couplets. Language: German (Upper German spellings: ai for ei, "kayner", "hain").
- Script: a bastarda/cursive book hand in black-brown ink. The first letter of every line is touched with a red stroke.
- Face 1 (image-001): the upper half is a framed, coloured pen drawing: a veiled, haloed woman seated before a cross holding the dead body of a haloed man across her lap, an open stone tomb behind, trees left and right. Below it 16 lines of text, opening with a three-line red initial I with pen-flourished knobs; the first three lines are indented beside it.
- Face 2 (image-004): 26 lines of text, no picture. Top margin blank, with paper repair strips at the top corners. Show-through of the picture frame and of the other face's text is visible. A pencil note written vertically at the lower right edge reads "MS TYP 220"? (modern; last digits uncertain).
- No running title, rubric, underlining or gloss is visible.
- Tentative interpretation only: the text addresses the woman of the picture in the second person and continues from face 1 to face 2 without a break in sense, so face 1 appears to precede face 2.

SELECTED AREAS: the whole text of both faces was read; nothing remains unread. Line 1 of face 1 is visible only in the overview image-001 (the tile image-002 begins at line 2).

Conventions: long s written s; v/u and i/j as on the page; ē = e with abbreviation stroke; ? after an uncertain reading.

=====================================================
FACE 1 (under the picture)
=====================================================
(overview numbering: text lines of image-001 counted from the first text line under the picture)
image-001 text l.1   Ich man dich magt erbarmerin   [red initial I, three lines high]

image-002 l.1  des sibenden grosses schmertzē dein
image-002 l.2  vnd hertzen laides vngemach
image-002 l.3  Das dir an deynem kind beschach
image-002 l.4  Do sich vollendet alles das
image-002 l.5  vnd er an dem creutz erstorben was
image-002 l.6  Joseph ain reicher gerechter man
image-002 l.7  Den man gen got in forcht sach stan
image-002 l.8  Edel genant von aromati
image-002 l.9  Der stund auch cristem? gelauben bey   [cristem or cristen; minims ambiguous]
image-002 l.10 vnd was sein iunger hainlich doch

image-003 l.1  Der stund auch cristem? gelauben bey   [overlap = image-002 l.9]
image-003 l.2  vnd was sein iunger hainlich doch   [overlap = image-002 l.10]
image-003 l.3  wan er forcht die iuden auch
image-003 l.4  pilatum · der da bitten began
image-003 l.5  das er im gab den toten man
image-003 l.6  den nam er von dem creutz her ab
image-003 l.7  vnd wolt in legen in sein grab

=====================================================
FACE 2
=====================================================
image-005 l.1  Do er in her ab genomen het
image-005 l.2  In dein schos man dir in let
image-005 l.3  Do wart erst dein iamer gros
image-005 l.4  Mit haissen zahern in begos
image-005 l.5  Die dir von augen gingen ab
image-005 l.6  Du spracht o meyns alters stab
image-005 l.7  vnd meyner augen groste wún?   [last word: w + minims with a superscript mark; wún/wunn]
image-005 l.8  vnd meynes hertzen liechte sún?   [sún/sunn]
image-005 l.9  wie hast du mich so hie verlan
image-005 l.10 Nu mús ich hie in trawrn stan   [bottom of tile; fully visible as image-006 l.3]

image-006 l.1  vnd meynes hertzen liechte sún?   [overlap = image-005 l.8]
image-006 l.2  wie hast du mich so hie verlan   [overlap]
image-006 l.3  Nu mús ich hie in trawrn stan   [overlap]
image-006 l.4  ye mer vnd mer wúchs der schmertz
image-006 l.5  Das die saufzen an das hertz
image-006 l.6  Stiessen das es todes begert
image-006 l.7  vnd das her symeones schwert
image-006 l.8  Dein leib hertz vnd sel verschnaid
image-006 l.9  In dem selben grossen laid
image-006 l.10 Tet dir got ain zaichen kúnd
image-006 l.11 Das sein leib zu der selben stúnd
image-006 l.12 wart hail weis vnd sauber gar
image-006 l.13 Das man kayner wūden wart gewar
image-006 l.14 wan die fúnff wūden fron

image-007 l.1  wart hail weis vnd sauber gar   [overlap = image-006 l.12]
image-007 l.2  Das man kayner wūden wart gewar   [overlap]
image-007 l.3  wan die fúnff wūden fron   [overlap]
image-007 l.4  Die sach man da offen stan
image-007 l.5  Do er gelet wart in den stain
image-007 l.6  Johānes fürt? dich mit im hain   [fúrt/fuert; superscript over u]
image-007 l.7  Do er dein in dem haus pflag
image-007 l.8  Das tet er treulich mengen tag ·

LIMITATIONS
- The leaf is clean and the hand clear; the readings are secure apart from the points marked ?.
- The marks over u (ú here) are a small superscript stroke or hook; I have not distinguished u-diacritic from umlaut, and in "wún"/"sún" I cannot tell whether a second n is abbreviated.
- "aromati" (image-002 l.8) is spelled so on the page; I have not normalised it. "fron : stan" (image-006 l.14 / image-007 l.4) is the rhyme as written.
- Face order is inferred from sense only; no foliation is visible. The text neither begins nor ends with a visible heading or explicit, so what precedes face 1 line 1 and follows face 2 line 26 is unknown from these images.
- This is an unverified image reading.
